subject: Board 16->24 of 46, and a stale file that was grading results against too lenient a bar
body:
Seventh version. Progress on the backlog I flagged last time, plus one thing you should
know about because it affected how results were being graded.

THE BOARD MOVED. Automated coverage went from 16 criteria to 24 of the real 46, and automated MET
went from 7 to 10.

    newly MET      C5.4, C2.5, C3.4
    newly NOT MET  C2.1, C2.3, C3.1
    still on prose 18

Four of those six already had working instruments. They produced counts and never a verdict, so
nothing read them and the board could not see them. From the board's side, a measurement with no
verdict attached is the same as no measurement.

C5.4 (conviction sizing bounded between 0.5 and 1.0) I earned on better evidence than the criterion
asks for. It names "the sizing log" -- but a log shows the values that happened, and the source
shows the values that are POSSIBLE. Every write to that multiplier is provably inside the range, so
no run can contradict it.

C2.1 is not met and not narrowly: there are 842 direct Print calls outside the log emitter. Each one
can put a line in the log with no block, no sequence number and no human line -- which is the entire
structure the C2 group rests on.

NOW THE THING YOU SHOULD KNOW.

C3.4 requires that statistical results be deflated by the total number of tests read from the test
ledger. There is a record file holding that correction. It said 176 tests and a critical threshold
of 3.629. The ledger actually holds 899 tests, and the correct threshold is 4.031.

The script that maintains that file had been APPENDING its results without refreshing the numbers
those results were judged against, so they froze on the day the file was created two days ago.

How bad is it: not bad, and I want to be precise rather than reassuring. Every result I reported in
the last week recomputed the threshold live rather than reading that file, so no published
conclusion changes and nothing is retracted. The artefact was wrong; the conclusions were not. But
a file sitting in the evidence folder claiming a 3.629 bar is exactly the sort of thing that gets
quoted later, and it would have made borderline results look significant when they are not.

Fixed, and the check I wrote for C3.4 now compares the record against the live ledger rather than
just confirming a record exists -- which is what caught it.

ONE NICE CONFIRMATION. Last version I told you the high threshold constants (82-90) admit almost no
bars. Tonight run 5's own rescue sweep printed its results at thresholds 50 through 70: six trades
at 50, and ZERO at 55, 60, 65 and 70. The EA found that from live data; I found it from the export's
score distribution. Same answer by two independent routes.

Run 5 is still going, now at the ghost rescue stage.
